initial_edits.rooks:
Use case: scientific-educational, illustration-story. The supplied image is the EDIT TARGET; PRESERVE the approved colored pen-and-watercolor handwriting, ivory paper, indigo galaxy, planets, and recognizable burgundy protagonist. Reformulate the demonstration of TWO ROOKS so a child immediately understands their straight-row/straight-column attack. REMOVE THE QUEEN completely and fill her former upper-right area with the same painted galaxy and stars, no new character.
Replace the disconnected arbitrary and half-colored marble blocks with ONE coherent suspended FIVE BY FIVE checkerboard platform. Its interior is a regular aligned chess grid, alternating a whole ivory square and a whole charcoal square in BOTH directions. Each cell has ONE base color; never split a tile into black and white regions. Fine marble veins are allowed but never obscure the checkerboard. Broken edges and loose chips only around the outside perimeter, not breaking interior grid alignment. Use a shallow elevated viewpoint so the cell pattern is very easy to read.
Show exactly TWO clearly identifiable dark rook chess pieces with crenellated tops on different squares, one near the upper-left part of the grid and another near the lower-right part; do not substitute castle buildings. Depict each rook's attack as THIN STRAIGHT OCHRE PAINTED PATHS from that rook's base extending along the CENTERS of its own row and column on the board, turning nowhere. Lines must align with the square rows and columns. No chain, no rope, no diagonal attacks, no curved arc between rooks, no floating connection mistaken for attack. Add very small drawn arrowheads at path ends if needed to make straight direction clear, not UI labels. Make these orthogonal paths unmistakable without flooding cells with gold.
The protagonist remains as an observer on a small foreground fragment outside the demonstration grid, similar pose and cloak to the original. This is an atmospheric handmade cosmic book illustration AND an accurate simple demonstration, not a screenshot or flat vector infographic. Keep ink hatching, irregular watercolor pigment, muted indigo, burgundy, ivory and ochre; do not smooth into digital 3D or change the illustration style. No Queen, no lettering, no labels or numbers.

initial_edits.bishops:
Use case: scientific-educational, illustration-story. The supplied artwork is the EDIT TARGET and its pen-and-watercolor style, cosmic palette and narrative composition are approved. Make the requested teaching corrections while retaining the burgundy protagonist at lower left, planets at upper right, indigo hand-painted nebula, ivory paper edge and floating broken-platform aesthetics.
REMOVE THE QUEEN completely from the upper left, including feather eyes, face and clothing; fill with the surrounding ink stars and watercolor space.
REPAIR THE BISHOP: make ONE elegant recognizable traditional chess bishop. Its upper form is a smooth rounded teardrop/mitre with ONE narrow clean diagonal notch near the top, a graceful neck and turned round base. NOT two enormous forked prongs, no weird jagged beak, no horns. Ivory and dark marble with a slender antique-gold local orbital ring are fine; preserve handmade drawing and material hatching.
MOST IMPORTANT — CORRECT THE CHECKERBOARD AND DIAGONALS. Below it show ONE coherent FIVE-BY-FIVE grid with straight aligned square rows, a shallow elevated near-top-down view. Starting upper-left cell is IVORY, alternate IVORY / CHARCOAL across every row AND down every column. Exact parity:
row 1: light dark light dark light
row 2: dark light dark light dark
row 3: light dark light dark light
row 4: dark light dark light dark
row 5: light dark light dark light.
ONE uniform base color per tile; no large black stains on ivory tiles, no half-black/half-white cells, no random repeated colors. Fine restrained marble veins, broken perimeter and loose chips are preserved.
Place the bishop on the CENTER LIGHT square (third row, third column). Draw exactly FOUR straight thin ochre rays from the center of that square, following the DIAGONAL LIGHT SQUARE CENTERS toward the four corner light squares. Each ray steps one row and one column together; it must visibly cross only same-color light square centers. The four paths make an X ON THE GRID, not a horizontal/vertical cross. No attack line along a row, no ray starting outside the bishop's cell, no random gold stripes. Small arrowheads at the distant ends may clarify direction. Keep squares visible beneath the thin rays. This must be an accurate easy-to-understand bishop-diagonal demonstration in the approved physical ink and watercolor style, without labels, letters, Queen or a game interface.
